input.summary: parts/shell.mjs builds the stone plinth, brick walls for the house and workshop, quoins, a stripped-oak head beam over the front, and the floors (y=1 and y=6 with the stairwell hole). It also builds the partitions, the four-step dark oak stair and every opening. The reserved cells stay air. make.sh gives 615 cells for this part with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks. All seven rooms are reachable, but I only read the walk output for the first three.
left: Stairs: the cells under the stair at x=16 are open air, and I did not look at them in a render. I also did not run the render or tile review, only check and walk.
I built the front head beam myself: stripped_dark_oak_wood axis x at (6..16, 5, 8). The plan assigns it to no part, so the facade part should not rebuild it.
I built a stone_brick_slab (top) sill outside the kitchen window at (18,2,14..15).
Upstairs I added partitions: spruce_planks at z=13 with doorways at x=8 and x=13 (y=7..8), and at x=11 for z=14..16. The ground partition at x=12 is dark_oak_planks.
The transom (7,4,8) and the lintel cells at (17,4,11..12) are left as air for fittings and chimneys. Door, window and firebox cells are all air.

waste.what: Listed door and window holes as boxes and filtered every wall cell against them, because the wall helpers have no opening-aware wall.
waste.cost: about 15 hole boxes written by hand
waste.tool: a wall(g, box, block, holes[]) helper in the vocabulary

waste.what: Worked out which corner and direction each quoin call needs.
waste.cost: 10 quoin calls, plus a first pass that skipped them because quoins only write into air
waste.tool: a quoinCorners(g, box) helper that wraps all four corners of a rectangular wall ring

waste.what: The B helper is not exported by vocab.mjs, so I imported it from the library by absolute path.

companions.task: The stair at x=16 and the stairwell rail, plus the support beneath the flight.
Lintel arches over the doors and windows, which I left as plain brick.
